bounded_statement: In this case only, each of the twelve first-collection source items identified by k1 (u01 through u12) appears in exactly two staged rows, contributing two `a` measurements each; the workflow feeds all 24 `a` entries into scipy's ttest_ind, a procedure that treats every row entry as an independent observation, and the report's df of 46 confirms all repeated per-unit entries were counted as independent. The reported p-value of 0.3953 therefore rests on an inflated effective sample size for the `a` side.

counterevidence_considered.description: The k2 codes are all distinct (v01 through v24), so the `b` side has no repeated units; the issue is demonstrated only on the `a` side. This limits the scope of the defect but does not negate it, since ttest_ind's independence assumption is violated by either sample.

One could argue the task's instruction to apply the procedure to 'the complete staged row sequence' authorizes using all rows; however, that instruction governs which rows are in scope, and it does not change the fact that the same identified unit's measurements were entered repeatedly into a procedure whose validity rests on one independent entry per unit.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: The task defines k1 as identifying the first-collection source item measured by column `a`, making k1 the unit identifier for the left sample.

evidence.description: Each k1 code appears exactly twice: for example u01 appears on the first two data rows with two different `a` values (1.0 and 1.5); the same doubling holds for u02 through u12 across the 24 rows.
The workflow builds the left sample from every row's `a` value with no per-unit aggregation and applies ttest_ind, which assumes each entry is an independent observation.
The report's df of 46 (24+24-2) shows all 24 per-row entries per side were counted as independent observations, i.e., the twelve k1 units were each counted twice on the `a` side.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to defeat the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways: (1) checking whether the repeated k1 codes might be typographical coincidence — they are not, since the task explicitly states k1 identifies the measured source item and every one of the twelve codes recurs exactly twice in a systematic layout; (2) checking whether the workflow deduplicates or aggregates per unit before testing — it does not, it maps every row directly into the sample lists; (3) checking whether the report might reflect a deduplicated run — the df of 46 proves all 24 entries per side were used. All three falsification routes failed, so the verdict stands.

root_cause: The workflow passes the raw per-row `a` column directly into a row-independent two-sample t-test without aggregating or otherwise accounting for the fact that the task defines k1 as identifying the measured source item and each k1 code recurs twice, so repeated measurements of the same authorized unit are entered as if they were distinct independent units.
